drivingQuestion: Why does the mishna restate that one gives and receives rights?

segments.he: סֵיפָא אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ: שְׁנַיִם נוֹתְנִין רְשׁוּת. הָא נָמֵי פְּשִׁיטָא! מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «He needed» it due to the ruling in «the latter clause,» which includes the novel teaching that «two» residents «may give away rights» in a domain. The Gemara again wonders: But «this» halakha «as well,» that even multiple residents may give away their rights in a domain, is «obvious.» The Gemara answers: This was stated «lest you say:»

segments.he: לִיגְזַר דִּילְמָא אָתֵי לְבַטּוֹלֵי לְהוּ. קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן.
segments.en: «Let us issue a decree» that two residents may not give away their rights in a domain, «lest» people «come to renounce» their rights «in favor» of two residents as well. People might assume that just as two may give away their rights to one, so too may one give away his rights to two. The mishna therefore «teaches us» that we do not issue such a decree.
